clusters.title: [Impact] dwm-wpf on Config2 - DWM composition may affect WPF rendering
clusters.body:
<!-- impact:dwm-wpf:Config2 -->

Impact analysis conducted on source code version:

- https://github.com/defrances/HostApplication - commit `22b249a754b849dac151e976b533f60994fc6098`

## Updates applicable for this product configuration

| Title | Package | CVEs | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Microsoft DWM Core Library Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability | [KB5093998](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-45637) | CVE-2026-45637 | Install - High Prio |
| Desktop Window Manager Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability | [KB5099535](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-50692) | CVE-2026-50692 | Install - High Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: `Config2`
- Model / role: `LabBench-L110` / `lab-analysis-workstation`
- Deployment group: `lab-ring-0`
- OS: `Windows 11 IoT Enterprise` build `10.0.26100.4200`
- Clinical criticality: `high`
- Network exposure: `restricted_lan`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `H` | `M` | `H` |
| Product | `L` | `L` | `L` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

Desktop Window Manager composition used when WPF presents the main window. Evidence on `main`: `src/HostApplication/MainWindow.xaml` (WPF visual tree) and `src/HostApplication/app.manifest` (`PerMonitorV2` DPI awareness).

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** The self-contained publish in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`--self-contained true` for `win-x64`) does not load this Windows component as a product `PackageReference`; Host Application starts without this KB.
- **If we install: App may break.** DWM cumulative updates can change composition or privilege boundaries; WPF presentation in `MainWindow.xaml` flows through DWM on the host.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Host DWM remains vulnerable while the product process can still start.
- **Compatibility: Compatible with the app.** Existing builds already run against the lab host DWM version; installing the KB patches the OS compositor, not files inside the self-contained publish output.

### Conclusions

These kernel/compositor updates change host windowing bits WPF relies on; they do not replace the bundled .NET 9 runtime inside the self-contained package.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

DWM EoP CVEs are in the Windows Desktop Window Manager component. SBOM and project files show no DWM library reference—only WPF UI that relies on the host compositor. This patch set addresses CVE-2026-45637, CVE-2026-50692. SBOM scan and source code scan show no matching dependency in product code; host exposure remains if skipped.

## Product Risk assessment

- Functions touched: Primary UI (`MainWindow`), status bar, and notes panel depend on WPF rendering through DWM; core file/TLS logic is unchanged.
- Potential hazards: None identified for this product configuration beyond generic OS regression risk after reboot.
- Install vs skip: Installing may require validation of WPF/UI or launch behavior; skipping leaves host-level exposure without stopping the product process.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- None. No documented test covers this coupling.

### Gap Analysis

- No automated UI verification after OS graphics stack updates.

## Recommendation

Complete lab validation per design control before any deployment adapter; table recommendation: **Install - High Prio** for host hardening where policy allows, with smoke/regression on notes and bulletin paths after reboot.

Impact analysis conducted on source code version:

- https://github.com/defrances/HostApplication - commit `22b249a754b849dac151e976b533f60994fc6098`

## Updates applicable for this product configuration

| Title | Package | CVEs | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows NTFS Remote Code Execution Vulnerability | [KB5099444](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-50448) | CVE-2026-50448 | Install - High Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: `Config2`
- Model / role: `LabBench-L110` / `lab-analysis-workstation`
- Deployment group: `lab-ring-0`
- OS: `Windows 11 IoT Enterprise` build `10.0.26100.4200`
- Clinical criticality: `high`
- Network exposure: `restricted_lan`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `H` | `L` | `H` |
| Product | `L` | `L` | `L` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

Local NTFS/profile file I/O for `%AppData%\HostApplication\notes.txt`. Evidence on `main`: `src/HostApplication.Core/NoteStore.cs` (`DefaultPath`, `Load`, `Save`, `ExportCopy`) and tests in `tests/HostApplication.Tests/NoteStoreTests.cs`.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** The self-contained publish in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`--self-contained true` for `win-x64`) does not load this Windows component as a product `PackageReference`; Host Application starts without this KB.
- **If we install: Compatible with the app.** The KB updates host NTFS filter drivers; `NoteStore` uses standard `File.ReadAllText` / `File.WriteAllText` and does not pin a specific NTFS driver version inside the published exe.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** The station NTFS stack can remain exposed to remote-code-execution class issues while notes I/O through `NoteStore` still works.
- **Compatibility: Compatible with the app.** Smoke test `TC-SMOKE-NOTES` already validates save/load on a temp path using the same APIs as production.

### Conclusions

Host NTFS cumulative updates patch the workstation file stack used indirectly by `NoteStore` BCL calls; they do not modify the runtime embedded in the published exe.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

NTFS RCE CVEs live in the Windows NTFS component. No NTFS driver is bundled; Core only calls BCL file APIs. This patch set addresses CVE-2026-50448. SBOM scan and source code scan show no matching dependency in product code; host exposure remains if skipped.

## Product Risk assessment

- Functions touched: Local notes persistence and export backup (`ExportBackupCommand`) use `NoteStore` file paths under the user profile.
- Potential hazards: None identified for this product configuration beyond generic OS regression risk after reboot.
- Install vs skip: Installing may require validation of WPF/UI or launch behavior; skipping leaves host-level exposure without stopping the product process.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- `TC-SMOKE-NOTES` — save/load round-trip guarded by `NoteStore.cs`.

### Gap Analysis

- None identified.

## Recommendation

Complete lab validation per design control before any deployment adapter; table recommendation: **Install - High Prio** for host hardening where policy allows, with smoke/regression on notes and bulletin paths after reboot.

findings.title: Vendor bulletin HTTPS accepts any server certificate
findings.evidence: On main, src/HostApplication.Core/InsecureVendorBulletinClient.cs AcceptAnyServerCertificate returns sslPolicyErrors == SslPolicyErrors.None (not unconditional true); Marker is TLS_CERTIFICATE_VALIDATED. tests/HostApplication.Tests/InsecureVendorBulletinClientTests.cs TC-REG-TLS-CALLBACK asserts rejection when SslPolicyErrors indicate an invalid chain. inputs/mds2.md MDS2-TLS still describes the old bypass and is stale relative to main.

findings.title: Notes stored as plaintext in user AppData
findings.evidence: src/HostApplication.Core/NoteStore.cs persists UTF-8 plaintext under %AppData%\HostApplication\notes.txt with no network export; inputs/mds2.md MDS2-DATA met (local notes only, no PHI). Residual risk is host-account access to the file, accepted for this PoC per catalog.

findings.title: No inbound network listener
findings.evidence: No TcpListener, HttpListener, or socket bind in application source; only optional outbound HTTPS via InsecureVendorBulletinClient.FetchAsync. inputs/mds2.md MDS2-NET met.
